bull_bear.body: Final dividend 20% proposed (plus 15% interim); Reinvestment in store network and brand building (Sennes); Debt reduction secondary to working capital needs for inventory.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Gold price volatility impacting consumer volume demand; Intense competition from national players entering East India and local unorganised discounting; Regulatory changes on gold imports/customs duties; Execution risk in non-East India markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Optimistic on long-term structural growth but prudently conservative on guidance; Emphasizes sustainability via old gold exchange and affordability (lightweight/lower carat); Acknowledges short-term demand softness in late May but expects recovery post-monsoon/wedding season.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Old gold exchange strategy aligns with government import reduction goals, creating a structural moat and ESG narrative; Inventory gains from customs duty hikes will flow through P&L over next 2 quarters, smoothing earnings; Sennes brand reached EBITDA profitability faster than expected (Year 2).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Equity raising history: "Raised INR 800 Mn equity from SAIF Partners India IV Limited (now Elevation Capital)" in 2015, "Raised INR 750 Mn equity from OIJIF II" in 2022, listing on NSE & BSE in 2023, and a QIP of Rs. 459 crore together with a 1:2 share split; both PE funds "Saif Partners and OIJIF II, monetized their investment".
- Vision 2030 return targets: ROE from 25.6% (FY26) to "20%+" and ROCE from 22.5% (FY26) to "20%+", with the CFO adding "a sharp focus on Return on Capital Employed (RoCE)".
- Stated financial priorities are margin and cash conversion rather than distribution: "Constantly Sharpen Profitability and Cash Flows" and "Generate robust Free Cash Flow for future expansion & working Capital need"; the CFO's focus list is "margin stabilization, improving inventory days, balancing finance cost through right mix of GML and optimizing subsidiary performance".
- The audited consolidated balance sheet shows Total Equity of Rs 25,136.8 Mn as at Mar-26 (Rs 19,702.9 Mn Mar-25, Rs 13,655.4 Mn Mar-24) against inventories of Rs 52,960.9 Mn, working capital borrowings of Rs 15,690.5 Mn and Gold Metal Loan of Rs 7,762.1 Mn.
- Franchising is framed as a return-on-equity device: "Franchisee store leads to higher ROE for Senco", with franchisee showrooms contributing "~33% of revenue" (proportion to revenue from operations excluding franchisee fees and discount allowed). The deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Senco Gold Limited is one of India's leading jewellery retailers, backed by over eight decades of trusted family legacy", with a "Comprehensive product portfolio across gold, diamond, silver, platinum, and gemstone jewellery for every customer segment" and "Senco Gold & Diamonds" anchoring a multi-brand portfolio.
- Strategy slide frames the moat as "East stronghold, national footprint" — "Deepen the 87-year East India leadership in brand trust and density, using it to fund and de-risk expansion into non-East and Tier III/IV geographies"; West Bengal alone accounts for 109 of the 209 showrooms (47 own, 62 franchisee).
- Fourth-generation promoter family business: founded by Shri Maran Chand Sen in Tanti bazar, Dhaka in 1938, moved to Kolkata after Partition; Shri Shaankar Sen (Founder Chairman) joined in 1979 and grew it to over 100 showrooms; Shri Suvankar Sen (MD & CEO) joined in 2007 and listed the company on NSE and BSE in July 2023.
- Brand credentials cited include "2nd most trusted brand award by TRA Research in 2025", "MCX Best Hedger Award", "Entry into the Deloitte list of top 100 global Luxury brands", "Franchisor of the Year Award 2025" and "Great Place to Work Certificate 2025"; ICRA rating shown as "A+ (Stable)".
- Scale markers on the Business Highlights slide: 18 States & UTs, 133 Towns & Cities, 87+ years of legacy, 3.24 Mn+ loyal customers, 300k+ designs, 3,324+ team strength and 66% footfall conversion.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Hedging policy] A detailed gold-price risk framework: daily rate fixing of old gold, trading jewellery and GML "for the equivalent amount of gold sold ... ensures that there is no cash loss or business losses"; sales hedging at 90%-110% daily/weekly and inventory hedging at "~50% of gold inventory value as per board policy"; instruments are unfixed GML (~10% to ~40% of gold inventory, which "acts as a hedging instrument") and MCX Futures & Options sell positions (~10% to ~40%).
- [Hedge accounting] "Senco's hedge accounting is aligned with Ind AS 109 (IFRS 9)"; effective-hedge impact is "adjusted to inventory valuation through WACC method, thus impacting Gross Margin" while ineffective-hedge impact goes to other income/expenses. "Since Senco does not apply Cash Flow Hedge accounting, any reference to OCI or deferred recognition of hedge ineffectiveness is not applicable".
- [Customs duty] Management describes a customs-duty rise "from 6% to 15%" that caused demand contraction, and separately says "Indian gold prices are post-custom duty increase impact of 9%" with "The benefit of the custom duty rise ... likely to accrue over Q3, net of the impact of price fall due to the hedging level"; a footnote separately flags "one time adverse impact of custom duty reduction in FY25 which had been adjusted to Inventory and Gross Margin".
- [Labour code] "We have also considered full impact of Labour code in Q1 after detailed evaluation."
- [Subsidiary performance] "Business losses at SFL and SGJTL also affected consolidated profitability, while SGAPL continued to report profit" — SFL "is still in the growth phase and incurred losses" while the Dubai entity SGJTL "incurred losses due to extraordinary market situation in gulf based on gulf war and Hormuz imbroglio".
- [Regulatory environment] Sector regulation cited as mandatory hallmarking with HUID marking (mandatory from 2021, HUID mandatory from 2023), "Mandatory Hallmarking for 9 Carat Gold from July 2025", mandatory PAN for transactions over Rs 2,00,000, and Anti Money Laundering applicability with "CBIC designated as a regulator for the jewellery industry".
- [Industry sizing — deck contradicts itself] The strategy slide states "India's jewellery TAM: $90 Bn (FY25) → $130 Bn (FY30E), organised share rising 40% → 50%", while the industry section is titled "India's Gems and Jewellery Market likely to Scale to TAM of $ 162 Billion" and carries the figures 162, 106 and 115 (USD Bn) against FY25/FY26/FY30E. Both readings are recorded; they are not reconciled in the deck.
- [Market structure] India is described as "The 2nd Largest Jewellery Consuming Nation" at 26% of global consumption versus China 28%, "the 2nd largest gold market in the world", with 70% share of gold jewellery out of total gold demand, rural India at 60% of demand versus urban 40%, and gold jewellery falling from 84% (FY24) to 83% (FY29E) of the Indian market while studded rises 12% → 13%. West Bengal and Maharashtra each hold 17% of BIS-registered hallmarked gold jewellery retailers.
- [Technology stack] Eight-element digital framework listed as ERP driven organization, ISO Certification, Modern Digital Platforms, Centralized Network Management System, AI-Driven Customer Service, Data Driven Decision Making, 360° CRM platform and AI-Driven Martech, supporting an omnichannel "Phygital" hub-and-spoke fulfilment model.

deepdive.thesis: Senco Gold delivered a record FY26 with 33% revenue growth driven by 60% gold price appreciation and a strategic pivot to old gold exchange (50% of Q4 sales), though management guides conservative 18-20% growth for FY27 citing volume pressure from high prices and competitive margin compression despite operating leverage.

open.horizon: within the next 2-3 years from FY26
open.item: Sennes Fashion Limited, loss-making in FY26, is expected to turn profitable within the next two to three years as it achieves volume and market traction.
On a normalised basis the Company expects ROE and ROCE to sustainably remain above 16-17% during FY27.
The Company plans to bring inventory days down from ~183 days to the management target of 160-170 days through AI-driven forecasting and smarter inter-store stock reallocation in FY27.

FY27 growth is to come from calibrated showroom expansion with an elevated roll-out of franchise showrooms under the asset-light strategy, plus strengthening subsidiaries and showrooms in newer geographies.
The combined impact of subsidiary performance on consolidated PAT, Rs 66.60 million in FY26, is expected to reduce further during FY27.

open.item: Inventory and capital allocation in FY27 will be guided by a SMART framework - Strategic Stocking, Merchandise Monitoring, Assortment Optimisation, Replenishment Excellence and Technology-Driven Inventory.
A stated FY27 priority is to increase the proportion of Gold Metal Loans in the borrowing mix in order to optimise borrowing costs.
The Company is targeting inventory levels of around 160-170 days during FY27, against blended inventory holding of 186 days in FY26.
For FY2026-27 the Company will pursue calibrated showroom expansion with an elevated roll-out of franchise showrooms in line with its asset-light strategy.
For FY27 the Company is targeting a sustainable PAT margin of 4-4.5%.
For FY27 the Company is targeting an EBITDA margin of 7.5-7.8%.
For FY27 the Company is targeting revenue growth of 20% or more.
The total impact of subsidiaries' performance at the PAT level, Rs 66.60 million in FY26, is expected to narrow next year.

The Company will enhance the performance of lightweight and everyday-wear jewellery across the 22K, 18K, 14K and 9K categories and drive premiumisation through its studded and diamond portfolio.

Retail expansion is to continue via physical store additions and targeted e-commerce optimisation, with a broader geographical footprint so the Company is not overly exposed to any single territory's economic cycle.

risks.note: The Company states that profitability and margins are heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment, so any supply disruption during gold procurement or adverse movement in market prices is a material financial risk. Gold jewellery accounted for ~85% of total revenue in FY26. Mitigation is product diversification into diamond, polki and platinum, and new verticals in leather accessories and lab-grown diamonds.
risks.risk: Margin risk - profitability heavily reliant on the gold jewellery segment

risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, elevated inflation, global monetary tightening and a broader slowdown threaten to limit discretionary spending, a direct risk to growth of the gems and jewellery industry. Mitigation cited is a strong domestic core, retail and e-commerce expansion, portfolio innovation and a broader geographic footprint so no single territory's cycle dominates.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic risk to discretionary consumer spending

risks.note: The sector is characterised by intense competition from both organised and unorganised participants; failure to consistently deliver high-aesthetic, premium-quality products at competitive price points would directly threaten market share, revenue stability and long-term growth. Mitigation is brand equity, design portfolio depth, product innovation and brand amplification.
risks.risk: Competition risk from organised and unorganised players

risks.note: The Company flags that data privacy infringement would materially affect the business and any breach could lead to non-compliance with data privacy law. Mitigation is cloud-based storage, software upgrades and continuous system hardening in line with new data privacy laws; ITGC audits are conducted by the internal auditors to mitigate cyber fraud and error risk.
risks.risk: Data security and privacy / data-protection compliance

risks.note: Purchased electricity in jewellery manufacturing and retail outlets raises Scope 2 emissions, and transportation and supply-chain activity raises Scope 3; the Company notes lab-grown diamonds are carbon intensive and will affect Scope 3 emissions in the long term. Stated financial implication is negative - it increases operational cost. Mitigation is energy-efficient lighting and air-conditioning, electricity monitoring, and evaluation of low-carbon transport and renewable energy.
risks.risk: GHG emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, classified a risk)

risks.note: Water usage in offices and manufacturing is identified as a significant risk given potential water scarcity from climate-related water stress; stated financial implication is negative. Mitigation is low-flow fixtures, monitoring of water use and rainwater harvesting at selected locations.
risks.risk: Water stewardship (BRSR material issue, classified a risk)

risks.note: BRSR Section A reports 100% of turnover from one main activity - manufacturing and retailing of jewellery with lifestyle and fashion accessories - across 18 States and 1 Union Territory, with exports contributing only 5% of total turnover and international presence limited to a single country. Earnings are therefore concentrated in one product category and one domestic market.

BRSR turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 27.00% in FY 2025-26 from 24.20% in FY 2024-25 and 19.00% in FY 2023-24 (female attrition 32.00% in FY26), a structural retention pressure in a showroom-led, service-intensive retail model; permanent worker turnover by contrast is 1.00%.
